formal.revision_note: Existing endpoint statements and exact dependency pins are retained. Fixed-anchor additions now prove the second-call joint-injectivity bridge, uniform two-call descent with finite actual germ tests, N+1-step termination, integral affine S1 for finite principal-quotient deviation, and omega affine/S38/torsion-cyclicity corollaries. Arbitrary categorical-test correspondence, independent semantic review and human review remain open. Goldie extension: Goldie's theorem for simple right Noetherian rings (essential right ideals contain regular elements, right Ore condition for regular elements), Goldie torsion, regular common annihilators, escape and affine source selection in Goldie-torsion bimodules. Non-domain core theorem: Theorem A', A and Corollaries B, C.1, C.2 for simple right Noetherian rings with regular anchors and Goldie torsion.

items.title: Actual graded-symbol interface
items.notes: The ten fields encode the actual nonnegative associated graded: gr_n:F_n→G_n is linear and onto; ker gr_0=0; ker gr_(n+1)=F_n; multiplication is respected. The graded-algebra instance makes G the direct sum of the G_n. The data have 1∈F_0, not F_0=k, and no finite-dimensional-piece field. The theorem separately assumes Infinite k, IsSimpleRing U, IsDomain/IsNoetherianRing G and finite Krull dimension. Semantic equivalence to an actual associated graded uses these exact kernel/surjection/multiplication conditions, not a freely chosen symbol algebra.

items.title: Fixed-anchor finite-deviation affine S1 and omega consequences for actual module germs
items.notes: Actual R-op module germs only; correspondence with arbitrary categorical tests remains open. The second-call canonical epic test implies epicity of (fd,gdL) modulo J, hence joint injectivity on each retained critical Schur space; fdL=dC gives vL=0. Ordinary and activated pencils, the checked colon bound and a central scalar outside the finite exceptional union prove the uniform two-call DevLE e -> Small e step with every old finite germ test preserved. Starting at Small (N+1), N+1 steps give Small 0 and actual integral U,V. The plain finite-principal-quotient affine theorem and omega affine/S38/torsion-cyclicity corollaries are implemented. No independent semantic correspondence or human review is claimed.

items.notes: Domain case only: hypotheses [IsDomain R] [IsSimpleRing R] [IsNoetherian Rᵐᵒᵖ R], [Field k] [Infinite k] [Algebra k R]; (Reg_I) is `∃ s ∈ I, s ≠ 0` (regular = nonzero in a domain) and (Fin_I) is `Module.DevLE Rᵐᵒᵖ N (R ⧸ I)`. `fixed_ideal` states `I ⊔ principalRightIdeal (x + H*t) = ⊤` for every x and t ≠ 0; `fixed_anchor_of_fixed_ideal` derives `1 = d*U + (B+H*a)*d*V` with I = dR, x = B*d, t = a*d exactly as in §1. The induction invariant `IdealBound I e` is P(h) of §4 with the strict stratum Small e; `idealBound_step` uses one first call, the torsion equation f*b ∈ I (b ≠ 0), a second call with offset 0, tail t*b and the single unit test of R/J, the ordinary stability pencil (Lemma 3.6) for v = q_Q f and for all old tests, a nonzero central scalar outside the finite exceptional union and the inclusion (4.2) via invertibility of the scalar. items.title: Input I1 (Goldie) for simple right Noetherian rings, Goldie torsion, regular common annihilators and escape (Lemma 3.4)
items.notes: I1 is imported from the literature in the written note; here the used part is proved for a simple right Noetherian ring R ([Ring R] [IsSimpleRing R] [IsNoetherian Rᵐᵒᵖ R], zero divisors allowed; regular means `s ∈ R⁰`, two-sided non-zero-divisor, convention C2). Route: the classical Goldie argument (Goldie 1958/1960; McConnell–Robson §2.3; Goodearl–Warfield Ch. 5–6) specialized to simple rings, so simplicity replaces semiprimeness and nilpotency of the singular ideal, and right Noetherianity replaces finite uniform dimension and ACC on right annihilators: the right singular ideal is zero (`eq_zero_of_isEssential_rightAnn`), nonzero right ideals are not nil and contain a nonzero `b` with bR ∩ r(b) = 0 (`exists_good_mem`), an essential right ideal contains x with r(x) = 0 (maximal-element argument), r(x) = 0 makes xR essential (no infinite direct sum K ⊕ xK ⊕ ⋯) and x regular. Proved: essential right ideals contain regular elements (`exists_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isEssential`), the right Ore condition for regular elements (`exists_right_ore`, packaged as Mathlib's `OreSet (Rᵐᵒᵖ)⁰` in `nonempty_oreSet_op`), common regular elements of finitely many right ideals, R/I Goldie-torsion when I has (Reg_I), common regular annihilators of finite-dimensional subspaces, and Goldie torsion of critical section modules (`section_isGoldieTorsion`, via essential annihilators). Escape (Lemma 3.4) is `exists_smul_mul_not_mem_of_goldie` with route same as the note (common regular annihilator, simplicity, regularity); affine source selection over Goldie-torsion bimodules (`exists_affine_source_of_goldie`) reuses the pinned AlgebraicAnalysis linear-algebra lemmas. Not formalized from I1: the classical quotient ring Q as a ring of fractions with Q = M_s(D) simple Artinian, flatness of Q, and closure of Goldie torsion under extensions and direct sums. `IsEssential E` is the elementwise form `∀ y ≠ 0, ∃ r, y*r ≠ 0 ∧ y*r ∈ E`.

items.title: Theorem A' (fixed ideal) and Theorem A for simple right Noetherian rings with zero divisors (regular anchors, Goldie torsion)

paper.anchor: ## 4. The two-call descent (proof of Theorem A')

items.notes: Hypotheses [Ring R] [IsSimpleRing R] [IsNoetherian Rᵐᵒᵖ R] and [Field k] [Infinite k] [Algebra k R]: (S), (N) and (Z) with (Z) expressed as an infinite central field (equivalent under (S), as recorded in C5). No domain or Ore hypothesis: I1 comes from `goldie-simple-noetherian`. (Reg_I) is `∃ s ∈ I, s ∈ R⁰`; (Fin_I) is `Module.DevLE Rᵐᵒᵖ N (R ⧸ I)`; `t ≠ 0` and `a ≠ 0` may be singular; the anchor d is regular (`d ∈ R⁰`). `fixed_ideal`: `I ⊔ principalRightIdeal (x + H*t) = ⊤`. `fixed_anchor`: `1 = d*U + (B+H*a)*d*V`, derived from A' with I = dR, x = B*d, t = a*d (t ≠ 0 by regularity of d) exactly as in §1. Tests (`GoldieGermTest`) are actual module germs with Goldie-torsion finite-deviation targets and regular tails c (the note's tests have c in S); source selection is `exists_affine_epic_tests` (Lemma 3.6, tails t*c ≠ 0 by C2) and stability is `GoldieGermTest.pencil_finite`. `idealBound_step` is the colon-free two-call step of §4: first call; torsion equation f*b ∈ I with b regular (I1); second call with offset 0, tail t*b ≠ 0 and the single unit test of R/J; stability pencil for v = q_Q f and for old tests; a nonzero central scalar outside the finite exceptional union; inclusion (4.2). Statement equivalence relies on identifying Kdim with the library's `Module.DevLE` and tests of C_e with actual module germs (tests are an induction device; the exported A' and A have no tests). Build/axiom evidence only; independent semantic and human review remain open.

items.title: Corollary B, C.1 and C.2 for simple right Noetherian rings with zero divisors
items.notes: Same hypotheses as `core-theorem-regular`. B: `principal_quotient_finite_of_omega` (under Module.DevLEOmega Rᵐᵒᵖ R, R/dR has finite deviation for regular d, by left cancellation as in Lemma 6.1), `quotient_finite_of_omega` ((Reg_I) gives (Fin_I)), `fixed_ideal_of_devLE_omega`, `fixed_anchor_of_devLE_omega`. C.1: `prescribed_cyclic` (Module.Finite, `IsGoldieTorsion R M`, finite DevLE of M; ∃ h, span {x + op t • h} = ⊤ for every x and t ≠ 0), with (H_all) (`∀ d ∈ R⁰, ∃ N, DevLE N (R ⧸ dR)`) and omega variants; the induction of Lemma 6.2 runs over a finite generating set and uses Theorem A' with tail t*b, b regular. C.2: `two_generated_of_principal` assumes a ∈ I and that every y ∈ I has a regular s with y*s ∈ aR (the elementwise content of aQ = IQ used in Lemma 6.3) and proves I = aR + (y + h t)R with h ∈ I; `two_generated_of_regular` discharges that hypothesis for a regular a ∈ I by the right Ore condition. Partial: the existence of a with aQ = IQ for an arbitrary right ideal (via Q = M_s(D), I5), hence 'every right ideal is two-generated' without a domain hypothesis, is not formalized; C.3 and Remark 6.5 are not formalized.
